title: Quantum Versus Classical Recurrent Neural Networks for Solar Radiation Forecasting over Mali
content:
Forecasting solar radiation is crucial for the deployment of photovoltaic systems
and for supporting renewable energy and agricultural planning in Sub-Saharan
Africa. This manuscript compares the performance of two machine learning algorithms
for this purpose: a classical Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and a hybrid
Quantum Neural Network (QNN), applied to monthly SWGDN prediction across 20
cities in Mali using MERRA-2 data from 1980 to 2025. The QNN architecture,
comprising an LSTM feature extractor followed by an 8-qubit, 3-layer variational
quantum circuit with Pauli-Z readout, outperforms the RNN in 9 of 20 Malian
cities (45%). Notably, the quantum advantage is most easily noticeable in cities
characterized by strong seasonal variability, whereas the RNN remains competitive
in more arid, stable regions. These findings underline the potential of quantum
machine learning for regional climate forecasting.
